title: Duterte’s ICC trial: How to watch and follow the proceedings
summary: Former president Rodrigo Duterte's trial at the International Criminal Court begins on November 30, 2026. Here's how you can follow Rappler's coverage.

blocks.text: DUTERTE. Families of victims of the war on drugs under former president Rodrigo Duterte, along with human rights advocates, gather at the National Council of Churches in the Philippines in Quezon City on September 16, 2026, to watch the live stream of the International Criminal Court’s third status conference.
Jire Carreon/Rappler
Former president Rodrigo Duterte's trial at the International Criminal Court begins on November 30, 2026. Here's how you can follow Rappler's coverage.

MANILA, Philippines – Former Philippine president Rodrigo Duterte will finally face trial before the International Criminal Court (ICC) in The Hague, Netherlands after years of calls for accountability over his violent war on drugs.

The proceedings that will start on Monday, November 30, will put Duterte’s bloody anti-drug campaign under scrutiny. The charges cover alleged killings carried out by the Davao Death Squad when he was mayor of Davao City and those linked to his national drug war during his presidency.
Duterte has been detained at the ICC detention center since his arrest in Manila in March 2025.
Hearings for 2026 are scheduled to run until December 17 before the court’s winter recess. Proceedings will resume on January 11, 2027.

Rappler justice reporter Jairo Bolledo and correspondent Michelle Abad will be in The Hague to cover the trial. They will bring updates from the courtroom and report on activities outside the court and detention center.
Here are the ways to follow Rappler’s coverage and stay on top of the latest developments:

The trial will raise questions about accountability and justice that deserve careful discussion. Join Rappler’s Justice and Crime community to follow the latest developments and exchange views with other readers.

Through the Rappler app you can get notifications and real-time updates. You can also join conversations with Rappler reporters and members of the community. The app is free to download from the Apple App Store and Google Play Store.
Watch Rappler’s livestream of the trial and follow the proceedings as they happen. Our team in The Hague will also share video reports from the court and its surroundings.
For Filipinos following the case from home, the time difference will mean evening viewing. The opening sessions are scheduled to start at 10 am in The Hague or 5 pm in the Philippines.
It is important to remember, though, that the ICC livestream has a 30-minute delay. This means online viewers will see the proceedings begin at 5:30 pm Philippine time.
Check this page to find out more about the key dates and schedules related to the trial.
The trial will involve legal proceedings and decisions that may be difficult to follow. We’ll help make sense of them through our reports and explainers.

Bookmark this page so you can easily find all of Rappler’s coverage in one place. We’ll post breaking news and reports from our team in The Hague, along with explainers and analyses on the charges and the trial process. We’ll keep updating this page as the case moves forward.
Can’t follow every hearing or check the news throughout the day? Get Rappler’s coverage straight to your inbox.
Register for a free Rappler account and subscribe to our newsletters. You’ll receive updates on the trial and other important developments covered by our newsroom.
Covering a trial of this scale takes time and resources. It also requires journalists on the ground and a team working behind the scenes to verify information and explain complex legal proceedings.

You can help sustain this work by contributing to Rappler’s investigative fund or becoming a Rappler+ member. Your support helps us continue reporting on issues of public interest and holding the powerful to account. – Rappler.com
